text: The account balance and the provision carried, the asset facts, the route history, the case state and the WO rule package are consumed on their owners' published contracts, never as tables or views, and their operation names stay placeholders until the owners publish them; the rwb-decision read is reached as an activity on that owner's queue, as the connection matrix row S7 gives it.
why: Only rwb-source-data holds SELECT on the recovery.v_ace_* views and owns the interaction ledger under the default ruling, only rwb-case writes recovery_case, and only rwb-decision governs the rule rows. The legacy Data table names recovery_case, v_ace_account, v_ace_npa_asset, interaction, decision_log_entry and rule_row, none of which is this service's, while TSD S7 T5.2 publishes interfaces with no operation names, so no name may be invented. The plan's C and X rows are empty, so these rows are class C in fact and not in the metadata.

text: R-WO-05 is read once, by the story that builds the pack: RWB-S7-E6015-APP assembles the pack with its agent run and document index, and this story asserts the five facts the posting track needs, records the outcome and moves the write-off stage to PACK_PREPARED; it writes no second pack builder, no second document index and no second agent run.
why: FSD S7 A2.9.3.1 lists R-WO-05 among the rules of the posting feature while A2.3.3.1 lists the same row for the pack feature, and TSD S7 T4 holds one row and one target state for it. Two builders of the same row in one service would write the same state twice and could disagree on the pack content, so the row is applied once and the posting track consumes the pack. No source says which story owns the row, so the split is recorded rather than decided quietly.

text: write_off.decision_log_id is written with the identifier the local decision-record library returns, and the P7 ledger entry identifier is not stored on the write-off row; the ledger entry itself is written by rwb-decision on the shared decision-record topic.
why: DF-FIN-012 is described as 'the decision_log_entry this record belongs to' and decision_log_entry is P7's table, while DP-03 keeps a local record in the caller's transaction and P7 keeps the central ledger. Storing a foreign identifier the service cannot verify would be a value it cannot maintain, so the column carries the record this service writes and the ledger stays with its owner.

text: The balance, the provision carried and the asset facts are read on the rwb-source-data contract and the service keeps no SELECT grant on any recovery.v_ace_* view; DP-05 is satisfied by the consumed contract, not by the service's own ACE views.
why: Only rwb-source-data holds SELECT on the thirty recovery.v_ace_* views (Architecture v5 slide 8), and the legacy Data table names v_ace_account and v_ace_npa_asset as if they were the module's. DP-05 allows either the owner's contract or the service's own views, but the second option needs a grant this service is not given, so the contract is the only reading that does not break the boundary.
